title: Large workplace study finds AI coding gains can stall at code review
friendlyTitle: AI helped teams write more code, but reviews became a bottleneck
summary: A working paper using roughly 300 million work events across 718 firms found that coding assistants and agents increased coding activity, with larger gains after agent adoption. Those gains did not translate one-for-one into completed software: review took longer, more updates required revisions and review comments increased.
friendlySummary: A large study found that AI tools increased coding activity across hundreds of companies. Finished software did not rise by the same amount because reviews took longer and more changes needed revision.
whyItMatters: Buying faster code generation does not automatically make a software organisation faster. Teams may need to invest in review capacity, tests, smaller changes and quality measurement—or simply move the bottleneck downstream while producing more code.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Writing code faster does not help enough if checking it becomes slower. Teams need better tests, smaller changes and enough skilled reviewers to turn extra code into useful software.
